synopsis_paragraphs: TOUGEN ANKI: Nikko Kegon Falls Arc (Tougen Anki: Nikko・Kegon no Taki-hen / 桃源暗鬼 日光・華厳の滝編) episode 1 sits in the cour’s opening contract with the audience. This is not a plot dump. The public catalog pitch is only a floor: After battling in Kyoto and Nerima, the Rasetsu Academy students have grown stronger.

But Yaoroshi leaves the academy to join the Oni Brigade for their "the total eradication of the Momotaro."  When Shiki realizes that they also target noncombatants, he sets out after Yaoroshi to bring him back. Meanwhile in Nikko, there's a research facility for horrific experiments atop the old Kegon Falls…  (Source: REMOW) What the week actually asks is whether Studio Hibari used that floor as architecture or as wallpaper. Genres on the tin read Action, Mystery, Supernatural; the useful question is which of those labels got camera time and which were merchandising. Community score currently hovers around 71, which tells you heat, not craft. We read the episode as a turning-point document: who gained a new obligation, who lost a convenient lie, and whether the cour’s theme got more expensive. TOUGEN ANKI: Nikko Kegon Falls Arc is being watched as a live product of manga adaptation. Japanese viewers argue about pacing against the source and about whether new episodes add a relationship change or only another demonstration of power. If you only remember a super move, you watched the trailer inside the episode. If you remember a silence, a blocked doorway, or a joke that hurt, you watched the show. Radar note unique to episode 1: this week we grade crowd and logistics: extras, radio chatter, the unglamorous walk between set pieces that tells you if Studio Hibari still has a world or only a battleground. Japanese same-night talk usually splits into people who wanted a trailer and people who wanted a scene. We side with the scene.
